newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil offered higher.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil offered higher.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run was offered higher at three figures but buyers were far below, while high sulphur Russian material rose on the back of crude and low avails.

Traders said the fate of a 25,000-tonne cargo of low sulphur straight-run loading July 5-10 marketed by a Norwegian major at $103 fob, or a few dollars over last done, will decide the direction of the market.
Buyers were heard around the $99 mark.
"The seller may take it into their own system because buyers are not in dire need of a cargo now," one trader said.

A U.S. independent refiner that has picked up three cargoes since late last week totalling some 75,000 tonnes was said to eyeing the early July loader, but the prompt loading date was seen as posing a problem for them.
"They have some 75,000 tonnes now and it would be more economical to take 100,000 tonnes (to the U.S.) but the (loading) date is too early," he added.
Traders said no other prompt cargoes were seem on the market.
High sulphur Russian straight-run was firm on the back of gains by crude oil and with little avails seen after several Russian cargoes were snatched up recently.
A Russian E-4 loading July 12-14 was heard traded at a strong three means plus $6.50, with one trader saying the price paid by buyer was due to "low avails and it feedstock that the buyer needs".
This compared with last done earlier this week at about three means plus $5.75/$6.
Two M-100 straight run cargoes fetched two means +$2 and +$2.50 respectively on Tuesday, and the former was re-offered on Wednesday with two other M-100 cargoes at about $4 over two means.

"The market is going up on the back of crude, and less avails and also the fact that the arb is partially open to the Med and widely open transatlantic," a trader said, adding three traders were moving cargoes there.
But a few other traders doubted deals would be done at those levels.
